checks.question: Does time instead grow after task launch with unchanged plan depth?
checks.inspect: Compare per-iteration input sizes, spill and hot keys in the Stages UI.
checks.action: Investigate skew or disk pressure rather than checkpointing every iteration. Checkpoint I/O itself has a cost.
checks.verify: Verify the dominant stage metric improves over multiple iterations.

records.reproduce: Run a bounded iterative RDD example with and without a periodic reliable checkpoint. Compare dependency depth and iteration time after materialization; check identical results.

records.title: One key dominates shuffle or group work
records.scope: Long duration alone is not evidence of skew. Check bytes, records and key frequency together.

checks.question: Does the long tail follow a key or partition across different hosts?
checks.inspect: Compare max/median records and bytes and a bounded key-frequency profile. Check whether a single group must fit together.
checks.action: Use partial aggregation where valid; isolate verified hot keys or use an eligible AQE skew join. Salting requires a correct second combine or join-side replication.
checks.verify: Verify result multiplicity and per-key totals plus a smaller slowest task, accounting for extra shuffle reads.

checks.question: Are byte counts comparable and only one host is persistently slow?
checks.inspect: Compare several partitions on that host and a matched task elsewhere; inspect GC, I/O and CPU stalls.
checks.action: Use slow-host diagnostics. Do not salt keys or change exact aggregations based on duration alone.
checks.verify: Re-run on comparable resources and confirm the slowdown follows or no longer follows the host.

records.reproduce: Profile a small dataset with one frequent key and many rare keys. Compare task-size distribution and per-key totals before and after an eligible partial aggregation or AQE join.

records.title: Shuffle parallelism does not match the work
records.scope: Initial shuffle buckets, final AQE reader tasks, and YARN container counts are separate controls.

checks.question: Are most reducers uniformly large and long-running, with idle slots available?
checks.inspect: Compare partition bytes/durations and actual allocated slots. Exclude one hot key and operators that require a single partition.
checks.action: Increase applicable shuffle parallelism before that exchange, or improve input layout. Do not use queue changes to split a deterministic single-partition operator.
checks.verify: Compare peak partition size, spill and stage duration at equivalent input size.

checks.question: Are most tasks tiny compared with scheduling and fetch overhead?
checks.inspect: Check scheduler delay, bytes per task, CPU use, and the final adaptive plan. A large number of buckets need not imply that many reader tasks.
checks.action: Enable or tune eligible AQE coalescing, or reduce excessive initial partition counts. Preserve required distribution and adequate concurrency.
checks.verify: Verify less scheduling overhead without creating a small set of large stragglers.

records.reproduce: Run a bounded groupBy with the same input at two sensible initial shuffle counts. Compare final AQE reader partitions, peak task size and scheduling overhead; keep executor capacity constant.

records.title: One executor is slow on otherwise comparable tasks
aliases: same partition fast on another host
records.scope: A slow machine and a large partition can look identical until host and partition IDs are separated.

checks.question: Are unrelated, similarly sized tasks slow on the same host?
checks.inspect: Compare input bytes, shuffle read, GC time, locality, attempt number and duration by executor across stages.
checks.action: Investigate that host with the operator for disk/network contention or memory pressure. Speculation can reduce tail latency but duplicates work.
checks.verify: Compare matched tasks after remediation and ensure external side effects remain safe for repeated attempts.

checks.question: Does slowness move with one partition rather than one host?
checks.inspect: Compare the same partition across attempts and sample data complexity as well as bytes.
checks.action: Follow skew, oversized record or CPU-expensive transformation diagnostics; replacing healthy nodes will not fix that input.
checks.verify: Verify the partition tail shrinks without altering the output.

records.reproduce: Use an event-log comparison, grouping comparable attempts by host and partition. A tail that follows a host suggests a different investigation than one that follows the same partition everywhere.

records.title: Input layout produces too many tiny or too few large scan tasks
records.scope: Input splits are determined by the data source and file layout before the later shuffle partition setting applies.

checks.question: Is planning/listing expensive and are files or read tasks mostly tiny?
checks.inspect: Inspect file count/size, listing time, scan partition count, and per-task duration. Account for source-specific open cost and grouping.
checks.action: Compact small files through a controlled rewrite or use appropriate source split settings; do not edit table-owned files in place.
checks.verify: Verify lower listing/task overhead with the same row and partition totals.

checks.question: Is one large input task reading a non-splittable file or an unusually large record?
checks.inspect: Check actual codec, file layout, row groups and input bytes in the first stage. A downstream repartition happens after this read.
checks.action: Use a splittable representation or rewrite into appropriately sized files; treat a single excessive row separately.
checks.verify: Verify the read stage itself distributes work, not just a subsequent shuffle stage.

records.reproduce: Write the same small dataset as many tiny files and as a compact file set in separate scratch paths. Compare planning time, scan tasks and total rows.

records.title: Scan reads more partitions, columns or rows than necessary
records.scope: Partition pruning, column pruning and storage-level predicate pushdown are not interchangeable.

checks.question: Are expected partition predicates absent or does the scan open more directories than required?
checks.inspect: Use formatted explain and actual file counts; inspect expressions, types, catalog metadata and dynamic pruning eligibility for the deployed version.
checks.action: Express the intended partition predicate in a form the source can use. Verify rewrites for nulls and dates before relying on them.
checks.verify: Check selected partitions and bytes read; confirm output equivalence.

checks.question: Are directories correct but ReadSchema is wide or data filters run above a UDF?
checks.inspect: Compare requested columns, pushed filters and Python evaluation boundaries. Source capabilities may limit pushdown.
checks.action: Project only needed columns and apply equivalent native filters before opaque transformations where semantics allow.
checks.verify: Compare scan schema, bytes, UDF input rows and output values.

records.reproduce: Use a partitioned test table, select only needed columns and compare a partition-key filter with a non-key filter. Inspect actual scan files, read schema and output values.

records.title: Tasks spend most of their time in regular-expression matching
records.scope: Investigate performance on benign bounded data. A busy task with little I/O is not automatically a regex problem.

checks.question: Do executor profiles repeatedly show regex matching on the slow records?
checks.inspect: Compare task CPU versus I/O and sample representative input lengths. Check whether the expression is interpreted by SQL, Python or the JVM.
checks.action: Replace unnecessary regex work with a literal/string operation or simplify the expression while preserving intended matches. Scope evaluation to the rows/columns that need it.
checks.verify: Compare match and nonmatch results, escaping, nulls and runtime across representative bounded inputs.

checks.question: Is apparent slowness actually an unexpected escape or match result?
checks.inspect: Compare the string that reaches the regex engine with the intended literal, including the SQL/Python string layer.
checks.action: Fix escaping at the relevant layer and add small positive and negative examples; do not assume one number of backslashes suits every interface.
checks.verify: Verify outputs explicitly rather than using a count that prunes the expression.

records.reproduce: Compare the original transformation against a simpler equivalent expression on bounded representative inputs including nonmatches, NULLs and escaped literals. Verify semantics before interpreting timings.

records.title: A benchmark action silently skips the expression under test
records.scope: A benchmark that counts rows may never materialize the projected column, UDF or problematic conversion.

checks.question: Is the target expression missing from the executed plan?
checks.inspect: Compare the optimized/physical plan for count versus an action consuming the target column; keep input and cache state identical.
checks.action: Consume a bounded checksum/aggregate over the actual values, or use an appropriate no-op sink for the exact runtime. Separate sink I/O from transformation measurement.
checks.verify: Verify the target operator executes, its metrics are nonzero and representative values agree.

checks.question: Do runs differ in warm caches, AQE decisions or cluster allocation?
checks.inspect: Compare input versions, final plan and executor resources before calling one implementation faster.
checks.action: Use a stable fixture and replicate warmed/cold measurements separately; report what the action measures.
checks.verify: Check the distribution across repeated runs rather than one elapsed time.

records.reproduce: Create a projected column and compare count() with an aggregation that consumes the projected value. Use the final physical plans to check whether each action executed the expression.

records.title: Find the stage responsible for a slow run
records.scope: Stage IDs can change between applications. Compare operations and data sizes, not raw stage numbers alone.

checks.question: Is elapsed time mostly before tasks run or while tasks wait for capacity?
checks.inspect: Align submission, AM registration, grants, executor registration and first-task times from both runs.
checks.action: Investigate staging or queue wait before tuning SQL operators. Ask for additional resources only if runnable tasks and eligible requests exist.
checks.verify: Verify time to first usable slot and pending-task duration improve.

checks.question: Is an equivalent scan, exchange or write stage slower at the same input volume?
checks.inspect: Compare final plans, task distributions, GC, spill, shuffle and output metrics. Separate global slowdowns from one outlier.
checks.action: Follow the corresponding scan, shuffle, skew or commit investigation. Change one factor at a time on a comparable snapshot.
checks.verify: Verify the specific stage and end-to-end runtime improve with the same output.

records.reproduce: Open the SQL and Stages views for a known-good and a slow run on equivalent inputs. Match operators, bytes and task distributions before comparing stage duration.

records.title: Write or subsequent scans suffer from too many small files
records.scope: Concurrent writer tasks, dynamic partition directories, bucketing and rollover can all multiply file count.

checks.question: Does file count track writer tasks times directories visited by each task?
checks.inspect: Measure data files per destination partition, size distribution, number of writer tasks and maxRecordsPerFile. Ignore marker files.
checks.action: Distribute by an appropriate output key and target file size, or compact using the table format. Avoid globally coalescing to one by default.
checks.verify: Compare files per directory, median size, subsequent scan time and full row totals.

checks.question: Does a single successful task create several files with incrementing counters?
checks.inspect: Inspect per-file row counts against the configured record cap.
checks.action: Follow case 40. Raise the cap only if rollout really is the cause and the resulting file sizes suit readers.
checks.verify: Verify fewer files without turning the writer stage into a straggler.

records.reproduce: Write identical rows to two fresh paths with different writer parallelism or rollover cap. Count data files and compute size distribution by destination partition.

records.title: Some output partitions finish long after all the others
records.scope: The table partition key and the Spark execution partition are different. Sorting alone does not necessarily rebalance task load.

checks.question: Does a late writer handle a disproportionately large date or key?
checks.inspect: Compare per-task bytes and the target partition paths, including the final AQE plan and table distribution requirements.
checks.action: Use a compatible repartitioning strategy that spreads hot data without breaking the table contract; local sorting changes order, not global balance.
checks.verify: Check max/median writer duration, partition directories, file sizes and result counts.

checks.question: Do tasks finish promptly but the driver lingers after the last task?
checks.inspect: Inspect driver commit logs and filesystem operations rather than adjusting reducer count.
checks.action: Follow object-store commit or job-commit diagnostics; use an appropriate table-aware maintenance strategy for existing small files.
checks.verify: Verify publication latency and read-back integrity separately from task runtime.

records.reproduce: Write a bounded dataset containing one hot date; compare per-writer bytes and elapsed time with a better balanced, table-compatible distribution, then reconcile all dates.

records.title: Object-store publication is slow or incomplete
records.scope: S3, Hadoop/S3A, EMRFS and table formats have different commit protocols. Directory rename is not a portable atomic transaction.

checks.question: Does time accumulate after tasks finish in copy/rename or job commit?
checks.inspect: Identify scheme, connector, committer class, table format and request metrics. Compare task output time with commit time.
checks.action: Choose a supported cloud-aware committer or transactional table writer for the deployed stack. Validate overwrite and retry support before switching.
checks.verify: Test success, a bounded aborted write and a retry on a private prefix; verify visibility and absence of duplicate results.

checks.question: Is commit fast but there are many tiny uploads or skewed writers?
checks.inspect: Compare file count, multipart/upload metrics and per-task duration.
checks.action: Follow file-layout or skewed-write diagnostics instead of changing commit semantics unnecessarily.
checks.verify: Compare throughput, file sizes and published record count at the same input volume.

records.reproduce: Write and read back a tiny fixture in a private object-store prefix with the supported connector/committer. Compare task completion timestamps to final publication; test retry only on scratch output.

records.title: Write action fails: locate the first failing boundary
records.scope: An exception at save() can originate in upstream computation, task write/commit, or job commit.

checks.question: Does the same expression fail before the sink is invoked?
checks.inspect: Use a bounded fixture and force materialization of the actual columns; a simple count can avoid the calculation. Check earliest executor error.
checks.action: Fix the upstream conversion, UDF or memory issue before tuning the committer. Compare the same input and plan.
checks.verify: Verify the projection materializes, then write and read back a new scratch destination.

checks.question: Did task data succeed but publication fail, or did the write never start?
checks.inspect: Compare task commit messages and job commit diagnostics with save mode, destination ACLs/quota and table distribution rules.
checks.action: Follow job commit for post-task failure or existing-path handling for skipped/rejected insertion. Inspect partial output before retrying.
checks.verify: Check committed visible files and expected contents rather than only successful task counters.

records.reproduce: Use the V1 failing-job-commit fixture from case 18 to isolate failure after task commits. Contrast with a projection error that fails before the sink gets valid rows.

records.title: Unknown or wrapped exception: preserve the first cause
aliases: Job aborted due to stage failure
records.scope: A top-level SparkException or Py4J wrapper is not a root cause. Keep uncertainty explicit.

checks.question: Is there a nested error condition or a task/container diagnostic earlier in time?
checks.inspect: Record the application and attempt IDs, SQL execution/stage/task IDs, first cause and which process emitted it. Compare one failing and one successful partition.
checks.action: Select the specific error by its class or message. Do not tune heap, increase retries or delete files solely from a wrapper.
checks.verify: Confirm the chosen diagnosis predicts the original evidence and a bounded reproduction.

checks.question: Is the first cause missing because the process terminated abruptly?
checks.inspect: Inspect YARN attempt/container logs, process exit status, available event logs and node health; redact secrets before sharing anything.
checks.action: Escalate to the cluster or data owner with versions, affected scope, timing, sanitized cause chain and a minimal fixture. Do not claim a fix without discriminating evidence.
checks.verify: Agree on a test that would separate the leading hypotheses, then repeat after collecting it.

records.reproduce: Reduce the incident to one application attempt and the smallest representative input. Record the first nested cause, not just the terminal exception; if logs are missing, document that gap.
